items.label: LightPath Technologies Q4 FY2026 (09-10-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CEO Sam Rubin on germanium substitution: China's first restrictions

set.signal: CEO Sam Rubin on germanium substitution: China's first restrictions on germanium and gallium exports in late 2024 started a growth in demand for BlackDiamond glass and systems using it; redesigns to BlackDiamond and new programs - whose design and qualification can take up to two years - are now beginning to move into production, and much of the recent backlog and bookings growth comes from them. He expects the trend to intensify because most customers did not start their redesign and substitution effort until well after the initial germanium export ban; new customers are being won both by converting them to BlackDiamond and by supplying assemblies and systems. LightPath has two domestic glass plants and, in his words, 'the broadest portfolio of infrared materials available'. On germanium supply he now sees more runway than he first thought: one of the leading companies noted current production of only three to four tons per year with increases several years out, and U.S. mining or refining awards also talk about single-digit tons, so he does not see new capacity solving the whole problem in the near term.

items.reason: Hedge restored: the CEO said he does not see new germanium capacity solving the whole problem near term, not that it will not solve the problem.
items.evidence: So while capacity is being developed, I do not see it solving the whole problem in the near term, and that likely gives us more runway.

items.label: LightPath Technologies Q4 FY2026 (09-10-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Capex was $6.3 million in fiscal 2026, $4.4 million of it in Q4

set.signal: Capex was $6.3 million in fiscal 2026, $4.4 million of it in Q4 - the last time LightPath spent at that level was calendar 2023, when it expanded the Orlando facility and doubled the clean room (CFO Albert Miranda). Fiscal 2027 capex will be higher than fiscal 2026, 'a deliberate choice made against a visible order book and pipeline' (CEO Sam Rubin); CFO: all locations will be expanded to meet the backlog and the demand foreseen through fiscal 2027 and into fiscal 2028, getting ahead of demand in key areas like BlackDiamond glass production. CEO on fiscal 2027: 'less about proving the thesis and more about scaling against it. Doubling a manufacturing business in 12 months is hard. Doing it twice in a row is harder, and it will require capacity we are still building and people we are still hiring.' CFO: the fiscal 2027 mandate is to add capacity fast enough, hold the margin gains and convert the book, and it is 'fully funded'. CEO: the company will also pursue accretive, capability-adding acquisitions similar to G5 and AMI.

items.reason: Attribution: the expansion of all locations through fiscal 2027 into fiscal 2028 and getting ahead of demand in BlackDiamond glass is the CFO's statement, not the CEO's.
items.evidence: Albert Miranda (CFO): ... We will expand all of our locations to meet the backlog we have and the demand we foresee through fiscal 2027 and into fiscal 2028.

items.label: LightPath Technologies Q4 FY2026 (09-10-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CEO Sam Rubin on other defense programs: in border tower programs

set.signal: CEO Sam Rubin on other defense programs: in border tower programs DHS has released funding to the prime, but it has not yet turned into camera orders; demand is growing instead for similar towers and cameras installed outside the U.S., primarily in the Middle East - mostly foreign military sales to allies for border towers in Middle East or North African countries, where LightPath is typically one step down with subprimes and each deal is usually 'in the tens of millions of dollars' for it. Air Force and Army opportunities are mainly counter-UAS and ISR systems. An unnamed airborne program has completed qualification and awaits the LRIP production order; the Apache program may make a comeback with renewed interest. Drone and drone-dominance programs are generating significant demand, which LightPath is meeting by adding automation for high-volume assemblies; two counter-UAS programs are transitioning to a cadence of deliveries of tens of systems a month. SPEIR cameras for the Navy: the first camera, or maybe two, have shipped and he believes another five are in dispatch, expected to ship in the next few weeks.

items.reason: Hedge restored: the CEO said he believes five more SPEIR cameras are in dispatch.
items.evidence: We did ship the first camera, or maybe two, and I believe we have another five cameras in dispatch before we get another order.

items.signal_prefix: Fiscal 2027 (initial outlook to be given next quarter). CEO tailwinds

set.figure: FY2027 capex above FY2026 (FY2026 capex about 3% of sales); CFO: 'still going to stay in that 4% or so'

items.reason: Figure clarity: 'about 3% of sales' is the fiscal 2026 capex level; as written it can be read as the FY2027 level, contradicting the CFO's 'that 4% or so'.
items.evidence: For your models, CapEx for fiscal 2026 will come in at about 3% of sales. ... next year we're going to be spending more CapEx than this year. But I do think we're still going to stay in that 4% or so.
